corrected_verdicts.note: The speed subcriterion passing does not make the CUDA gate pass. Section 10 requires a nonzero exit on NaN and 29 worlds went non-finite.

failure_taxonomy.note: Phase 3.4 collapsed these into one flag named worlds_ran_without_oom. 29 non-finite worlds are not 29 OOMs, and conflating them hides which cause is actually present.
failure_taxonomy.overflow_worlds: not_measured -- Data.overflow bitmask was never read

invalid_telemetry.reason: Measured with torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(), which only tracks PyTorch's allocator. Warp allocates through its own, so this figure measures nothing about the backend under test. It was reported as vram_within_budget=true, which is an unearned pass and is retracted here. The raw JSON is left unedited so the provenance of the error stays visible.
invalid_telemetry.replacement_required: device-level peak via Warp free-memory delta and NVML (P3.4.1-03)

open_questions_for_triage: Is Data.overflow set before the NaN appears?
Are the rejected indices stable across fresh processes?
Do permuted and duplicated worlds diverge at the same indices?
Which kernel or stage produces the first non-finite value?
purpose: Freeze the Phase 3.4 GPU evidence and correct its interpretation. Raw numbers are preserved unchanged; only the verdict wording is fixed.
